claims.text: Thermomechanical treatment can introduce a hierarchical microstructure containing nanosized precipitates into FCC high-entropy alloys.
A hierarchical microstructure with nanosized precipitates can improve the dynamic strength–ductility performance of FCC high-entropy alloys.
Nanosized precipitates provide additional barriers to dislocation motion.
Nanosized precipitates promote deformation-induced twinning in FCC high-entropy alloys.
Mechanical twinning is an important deformation mechanism in the FCC Al0.3CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy at high strain rates.
Dislocation slip and twinning under dynamic loading can produce strong strain-hardening ability in an FCC high-entropy alloy.
At cryogenic temperatures, deformation-induced twinning and martensitic transformation enhance work hardening in FeCoCrNiMo-C medium-entropy alloys.
The treated alloy will have greater yield strength than the untreated FCC HEA baseline under dynamic loading.
The treated alloy will have greater tensile elongation than the untreated FCC HEA baseline under dynamic loading.
The proposed improvement should hold at high strain rates.
The proposed improvement should hold at high temperatures.
The proposed improvement may not apply under static loading or different environmental conditions.
The magnitude of improvement may depend on alloy composition, processing conditions, and testing parameters.
A treated-versus-untreated comparison using yield strength, tensile elongation, and microstructural characterization can test the hypothesis.
Failure of the precipitate-containing hierarchical microstructure to improve dynamic strength–ductility performance would falsify the hypothesis.
